title: Hopper FP8 per-op scaling & telemetry-driven fallback for long-sequence stability (E4M3/E5M2)
creator: Avery Chen
description: Background: Enabling FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) on Hopper showed strong cost/latency benefits for short‑sequence generation, but we’ve observed accuracy drift and infrequent instability for long‑sequence workloads and micro-batched inference. Goal: implement per-operation scaling heuristics and a telemetry-driven fallback that (1) applies local per-op FP8 scaling factors for matmuls/attention kernels, (2) detects drift signatures in real time, and (3) gracefully falls back to INT8/FP16 on affected request slices. This ticket covers design, implementation, synthetic and customer‑facing evals, and rollout gating criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Per-op scaling implemented in runtime kernel dispatcher and configurable via model quant profile
Telemetry pipeline emits per-op scale histograms, kv-cache drift rate, and per-batch accuracy proxy metrics
Fallback policy that switches affected micro-batches to INT8/FP16 with <1% latency tail regression
Synthetic eval suite shows no >1.0% relative quality regression across long‑sequence benchmarks vs float32 baseline
Canary run on dedicated pool with 5k genus requests/day without new crash rate or >2% customer error uplift
Runbook and dashboard links added; rollout SOP reviewed by PM and SRE
tech_notes: Per-op scaling: compute a small (8‑bit scaled) multiplier per GEMM/MatMul op at calibration time; store as kernel metadata and apply to inputs during runtime to reduce outlier saturation
Micro-batching: maintain per-sub-batch scale histograms; do not aggregate across logically different prompts (e.g., mixed length) to avoid masking tail issues
KV-cache drift mitigation: detect sustained growth in prefix attention activations and trigger conservative scaling that biases to higher dynamic range for recent KV slices

Fallback heuristics: threshold-based on (a) scale histogram skew, (b) per-batch perplexity proxy delta, (c) runtime NAN/inf rate; fallback toggles to INT8 for the offending batch only and records event
Kernel selection: use existing kernel registry to tag compatible kernels for per-op scaling; add quick-path for FP16 fallback to minimize cold-start latency
Calibration workflow: extend existing calibration pipeline to emit per-op scale candidates and suggested hysteresis windows; store candidate seeds for reproducibility
Eval harness: extend golden-suite with long-sequence instruction following (8k–64k tokens), QA pairs, and summarization tasks; include both open and internal customer datasets where permitted
Telemetry: new metrics (scale_hist_{op}, kv_cache_drift_rate, per_batch_quality_proxy, fp8_fallback_events) to observability; tag by model, release, kernel_version, and host pool
Performance targets: avoid >10% throughput loss when fallback events are <1% of traffic; tail latency regression target <20% p99 increase for affected batches
Safety: add binary flag to disable automatic fallback per-customer in the private/Dedicated offering; audit all fallback-triggered requests
risks: Overly aggressive fallback could negate FP8 cost benefits—need conservative thresholds and adaptive hysteresis
Telemetry noise on low-volume customers could cause cascaded toggles—use per-customer smoothing and minimum sample windows
Calibration divergence across model versions may require per-version seeds and backward-compatible metadata
Kernel-level bugs in per-op scaling may cause subtle numerical regressions not covered by synthetic evals—need expanded golden-suite
comments: 2025-11-05: Triage meeting — scoped to runtime + telemetry + eval workstreams. Assigned to Marcus for runtime, Priya for telemetry, and Elise for evals.
2025-12-10: Prototype implemented for per-op scaling in local dev; unit tests for GEMM scaling added. Observed 0.8% avg delta on short-seq LMs, encouraging.
2026-01-12: Canary#1 on internal pool (small scale) — saw sporadic fallback events tied to very long contexts (>32k). Root cause looks like accumulated kv-cache dynamic range growth.
2026-02-20: Telemetry tuning — added kv_cache_drift_rate metric and reduced fallback sensitivity by increasing hysteresis window from 3 to 10 batches; fallback events dropped by 7x in canary.
2026-03-02: Eval update — extended golden-suite with two internal customer datasets (summaries and RLHF style prompts). Preliminary results show <0.6% quality delta vs FP32 on target configs.

2026-03-14: Preparing rollout plan: staged canary to dedicated pools (5% -> 20% -> 60%), monitoring dashboard and automatic rollback if fallback_rate > 0.5% for 1h or if per_batch_quality_proxy delta > 1.0%
